title: Tool-call atomicity: streaming handshake and deterministic result-injection API
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Adds a negotiated streaming handshake for multi-tool calls and a deterministic result-injection contract to reduce race conditions and improve resume behavior across OpenAI-compat layers.
commits: c7a9f2b: introduce streaming-handshake protocol and connector layer
d2b1e4f: add deterministic result-injector and idempotency token plumbing
f5e6b3a: telemetry + tests for concurrent tool call replay and resume
a1b2c3d: docs + examples for python/ts SDK usage
description:
Motivation: We continue to see flakiness and subtle ordering bugs when user prompts trigger multiple parallel tool/function calls while streaming responses. The core problem is a mismatch between streaming chunk boundaries and when tool results are injected into the generated token stream. This PR introduces a negotiated streaming handshake plus a deterministic result-injection contract (idempotent tokens + sequence markers) to make multi-tool streaming robust across the OpenAI-compat layer and SDKs.

Summary of changes: added a light-weight streaming-handshake protocol that runs as part of the connection init (client -> server -> ack) to advertise support for deterministic injection and per-call idempotency tokens; implemented a ResultInjector component in the serving runtime that accepts tool outputs annotated with an idempotency token and a sequence offset; modified the OpenAI-compat streaming adapter to honor handshake negotiation and emit compatible event frames ("tool_start", "tool_result", "tool_end", plus existing "data" frames); extended python/typescript SDKs with ergonomic helpers to 1) create idempotency tokens for tool invocations, 2) register callbacks that receive deterministic tool frames even when responses are replayed from cache or resumed after transient disconnects.

API/Protocol sketch (example): client sends: {"type":"handshake_capabilities","capabilities":["deterministic_injection","idempotency_token"]} server responds: {"type":"handshake_ack","session_id":"s_xxx","supported":["deterministic_injection"]} During stream the server emits: {"event":"tool_start","tool":"weather","call_id":"call_123"} then: {"event":"tool_result","call_id":"call_123","idempotency":"tok_abc","seq":1,"payload":{...}} Finally: {"event":"tool_end","call_id":"call_123"}. The SDK helpers rehydrate these frames into single tool-result objects and guarantee deduplication by idempotency token.

Design notes: - Atomicity: tool-result frames are applied at a single logical insertion point in the generated token stream (we record the insertion offset and apply deterministic replays). - Resume behavior: client reconnects present their last-observed seq/idempotency tokens; server can resume or replay exact frames without risk of double-injection. - Backwards compatibility: handshake is optional; if not negotiated the server falls back to pre-existing best-effort injection. The OpenAI-compat adapter exposes the new frames as extension events while preserving standard text/event-stream fallback.

Testing: added unit + integration coverage: - deterministic replay tests for the injector (including out-of-order arrival and duplicate delivery) - streaming handshake E2E tests between python SDK and local runtime - load test verifying latency regression less than 3% under multi-tool stress compared to baseline. CI initially flagged an intermittent test in streaming_adapter.rs; I fixed a race in the test harness and re-ran pipelines.

Docs and examples: console/docs/tooling/streaming-handshake.md contains a migration guide and code snippets for python/ts. Added 'tooling:experimental' note in console to avoid surprising GA customers.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime config (tools.deterministic_injection = off by default). We'll enable for a small percent of traffic for 48 hours and monitor: token duplication alerts, stream-error increase, and tool-latency percentiles. If stable we will flip the flag and remove the experimental note in 2 weeks.
review_thread: Arjun: Left suggestions around the handshake payload size and whether we need feature-discovery vs boolean cap flags. Suggested switching to an extensible key/value list. Author reply: switched to capabilities list and trimmed payload to ~128 bytes.

Samantha: Asked about cost/latency impact on hot paths and whether we can avoid copying tool payloads. Author reply: injector uses zero-copy when possible; benchmark shows 2.1% median latency increase under stress (within target).

Diego: Requested explicit tests for cache-replay + handshake mismatch (server older runtime). Author reply: added integration test that simulates older runtime behavior and verifies fallback to best-effort injection.
Arjun: Approved after small nits fixed
